property_summary: For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the reference increments proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant sometimes leaves the stored proposal under the old index and increments later, causing proposalCount_after to differ from expected and the mapping at the originally emitted index to contain a zero/old slot — the test checks that proposalCount increases by exactly 1 after the call.

For any caller, calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) increases proposalCount by exactly 1 and the mapping mapPID_grant at the previous proposal index (proposalCount_before) stores the provided recipient and amount; the mutant that increments proposalCount after storing/emitting breaks this because it writes the grant at the old index while emitting that old index and increments later, causing proposalCount and the stored grant/index relationship to diverge for some inputs.

For any caller and any (recipient,amount), calling newGrantProposal stores the grant at index equal to the proposalCount BEFORE the call and then increments proposalCount by exactly 1; the mutant that increments at the end can make the post-call proposalCount not equal to prior+1 for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For every call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) the reference contract always increments proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1) and stores the new GrantDetails at the index equal to proposalCount_before; the mutant that moves the increment to the end can cause proposalCount_after to not equal proposalCount_before + 1 for some inputs (specifically when proposalCount_before is non-zero and observations race with external reads), so checking the exact increment from an external caller distinguishes them.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) on the correct contract increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that moves the increment to the end can make that relation false for some inputs because it emits/stores using the old index and only increments afterwards.

For any call to newGrantProposal by any caller with any recipient/amount, the reference contract always increments proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that omits incrementing will violate this for some inputs (any call).

Calling newGrantProposal increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (for any initial proposalCount and inputs); the mutant increments by 2 and thus will make proposalCount differ from reference for some inputs.
